Subject: Cross-store authZ & retention test plan — Pinecone / Weaviate / pgvector

Hi all,

Thanks for taking this on. Greystone is starting a small production pilot next month and they need us to validate two cross-cutting areas before go-live: (1) authorization boundary preservation across vector stores + S3 backing, and (2) TTL / retention semantics for chunked embeddings stored across stores.

High-level ask: can each vendor run the attached sanity tests (sheet: crossstore-authz-test-plan-v1.xlsx) and confirm the following by 2026-09-14:
- whether object-level authz metadata (RBAC labels, owner_id) survives export/import and query-time joins
- behavior for expired objects when a vector index references S3 blobs (soft-delete vs hard-delete)
- signed URL / presigned-object flows for upfront uploads and on-demand retrieval from embedding pipelines

I've copied Ben and Neha from our integrations team to coordinate test harnesses and collect logs. Attachments: sample-manifests.json (example payloads), s3-signed-url-playbook.pdf (recommended patterns).

Next steps: Ben — can you share the test harness runner and where to send logs? Neha — can you scope an automated regression for retention?

Thanks,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Partner Eng, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Quick note on runner: we have a small harness in GitHub (interop-tests/greystone-runner) that will:
- push 10k sample embeddings (manifest in attachments)
- simulate role changes (3 role flips per object)
- emit an access log for each read that attempted to resolve a referenced S3 URL

I'll provision a sandbox bucket for each vendor (minio-backed) and share credentials via the secure channel. Logs will be collected to the runner's /logs endpoint.

Subject: Re: Cross-store authZ & retention test plan — Pinecone / Weaviate / pgvector

Thanks Olga — Pinecone can run the runner and we've scoped the work. A few clarifications from our side:
1) Pinecone metadata fields are limited to 1KB per vector; can you confirm whether "owner_id" will be stored in vector metadata or only stored in the manifest linked to S3?
2) For TTL behavior: Pinecone's native TTL deletes vectors but will not automatically delete externally referenced S3 blobs; we can add a lifecycle hook that fires a webhook on delete. Is Redwood able to accept a webhook to trigger S3 lifecycle?
3) On signed URLs: we can generate ephemeral keys in our sandbox; advise using short TTLs (30s) for on-demand retrieval tests.

We should also test race conditions where object ownership flips immediately after a vector read — Pinecone will provide hooks to emit read-intent traces so we can correlate with the runner logs.

I'll upload our initial run results to the sharepoint link by 2026-09-10.

Alex Chen
Partner Eng — Integrations
Pinecone

From: Sara Lind <sara@weaviate.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@pinecone.io>, devs@pgvector.org
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-store authZ & retention test plan — Pinecone / Weaviate / pgvector

Weaviate can run the TTL + S3 reference scenario. A few items to flag:
- Weaviate stores external references in the vector schema as "references"; we keep a pointer to S3 and a separate metadata map. If the referenced object is removed, queries that dereference can be configured to either return a partial result or fail the deref call. We'll run both modes.
- For authz: Weaviate supports token-based policies at read-time but does not natively replicate third-party RBAC labels to vector metadata. If the customer requires object-level RBAC enforced inside the vector store, we recommend a small middleware service that checks headers and rejects queries.

We will post our run logs and a short write-up by 2026-09-12.

Sara Lind
Partnerships
Weaviate

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-store authZ & retention test plan — Pinecone / Weaviate / pgvector

Hi team,

Summary of pgvector results (attached in-line):
- Metadata: pgvector (Postgres) supports arbitrary JSONB metadata; owner_id persisted OK and survived export/import and role flips in our test (no size limits beyond DB row size).
- TTL/Retention: pgvector test used a background vacuum job that handled vector deletions and a separate job to gc S3 blobs. We observed a ~30s window where a deleted vector could still resolve an S3 reference; recommend a webhook + confirm pattern for critical deletes.
- Signed URL flow: seamless; Postgres manifest stored presigned URL expiry and the runner validated download success with short TTLs.

Action items:
- Redwood: please wire the webhook endpoint for delete confirmations so vendors can call it to trigger S3 GC.
- Pinecone: confirm whether webhook calls will include vector_id + owner_id in the payload.
- Weaviate: include the partial-vs-fail dereference results in your write-up so we can codify expected behavior in the pilot SLA.

Thanks,
pgvector maintainers

--
